Tubes Cursor (WebGL, WebGPU) by Kevin Levron
Reference: https://codepen.io/soju22/pen/qEbdVjK
Catalog: https://freefrontend.com/three-js/#2026-02-05-neon-3d-tubes-cursor-trail-l
Runtime: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/threejs-components@0.0.19/build/cursors/tubes1.min.js

The referenced CodePen declares Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0:
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/
Its attribution and noncommercial/share-alike notice are retained for this adaptation.
The runtime bundle also includes the original Three.js MIT notice. Those upstream
notices are retained verbatim; this file does not replace their terms.

tubes1.min.js is an unchanged, byte-for-byte vendored runtime.
SHA256: 676abd6ccd18742a36dcb4ffce66a2052a4f203f240cd8cf97c6ea33a181f81b
V3 changes the initial tube and light color arrays only. Intensity, bloom, pointer
tracking, movement, rendering resolution and idle behavior use the original defaults.
The original random-colors-on-click behavior is retained in reference.js. The HTML
import map resolves its unchanged CDN specifier to the identical local runtime.
frame.html, bridge.js and the React host integrate the component into an isolated
disposable document, with matching pointer/click input and preference controls.
This contains the upstream bound-listener cleanup issue without altering the runtime.
